radar_guide_subtitle: How to find the exact desk of a Bluetooth device
radar_guide_step1_text: Walk slowly along one aisle of the exam hall and watch the banner at the top. The radar shows distance only, not direction, so you find the device by moving.
radar_guide_step2_text:
• Green — {closer}: you are heading the right way.
• Red — {away}: turn around or change aisle.
• Blue — {steady}: walk 1–2 m further and watch for a change.
radar_guide_step3_text: When the distance drops below about {meters} m and {critical} is shown, hold the phone close to each nearby desk in turn. The desk with the strongest signal is the most likely source.

rf_guide_step1_text: Live 2.4 GHz Bluetooth transmissions received by this phone, in dBm. It shows the strongest nearby transmitter, packets per second and how many devices are transmitting. A phone cannot measure cellular (SIM) signals directly.
rf_guide_step2_text: Walk slowly between desks. Above -50 dBm the transmitter is within about 1 metre: the meter turns red and beeps.
rf_guide_step3_text: A node is recognised only by a Bluetooth name starting with "ExamGuard". Any other ESP32 or DIY board is an unknown transmitter and may be a cheating device.

mag_guide_subtitle: Using the magnetic scanner in the exam hall
mag_guide_step1_text: Move the phone slowly within 1–5 cm of the candidate's clothes, pockets, collar, hands or desk. The phone's magnetometer picks up metal and magnets.
mag_guide_step2_text:
A normal room field is about 25–65 μT. Alerts use the change from your baseline (T = ±{low} / {medium} / {high} μT for low / medium / high sensitivity):
• more than T: metal or a small magnet nearby
• more than 2×T: strong anomaly — phone, watch or speaker magnet likely
• more than 4×T (or above 200 μT): device or magnet at contact range
mag_guide_step3_text: To filter out the normal field from metal benches and chairs, hold the phone in an open spot and tap "{button}". Readings are then measured against this room.
mag_guide_step4_text: If you find suspicious metal or a device, tap "{button}" to record it with the current readings.

hall_intro: Link several invigilator phones and ExamGuard sensor nodes in one exam hall. Everyone sees the devices and alerts the others detect.

hall_nodes_offline_hint: Check the node: power, hotspot and whether anyone touched it. It reconnects by itself when it can.
hall_node_step1: Power the node. First time, or to change settings: hold its BOOT button for 3 seconds until the light double-blinks.
hall_node_step2: On another phone (joining Wi-Fi can switch this phone's hotspot off), connect to "ExamGuard-Setup-…" (password: examguard). A setup page opens.
hall_node_step3: Pick this phone's hotspot, enter its password and the node key {key}, then tap Save.
hall_node_step4: Put that phone back on the hall hotspot. The node restarts and appears under "In this hall" with a solid light.
